title: Bob Wilber, royalties and recognition of composers
summary: Allen mentions Bob Wilber crediting composers; Rene discusses royalties and Louis Armstrong's recording of his songs.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: Well, I'll tell you, Bob Wilber's in town. Do you know him by name? He plays soprano and clarinet, and he studied with Bechet. Yeah. And he always, it seems to me, wants to give credit. He wants to do some of James B. Johnson's numbers. Yeah. He's coming up Wednesday. Is that so? He's playing at the Hyatt, you ought to hear him. Is that so? He's gone beyond copying Bechet or Hodges or anything like that. Oh, yeah, so. He's playing Milt Hinton's own bass. Anyway. Is that so? I'm going to ask. Just for a piece of it, but there are some now who are beginning to realize it, like him. He did a whole album of Bogey Carmichael numbers. That's good. That's good. You know, and, because, you know, who does recognize stuff like that?
That's right. Yeah. And it is their whole survival. I mean, survival of jazz, at least the making of it.
Yeah. At least you're getting the royalties, and they're not. That's true.
Well, we get the royalties. But you know the thing about it is almost the insult of it when you appear before them.
And won't even give credit to them. The guy's standing right before you.

And you play his song and won't say that this is the composer of the song. You see, I've had the biggest guys that really don't have no problem there. Yeah. But some of them don't realize the respect that's due. That's just like slapping your face. Say, for instance, taking something that you've done and don't even give you credit for it. And he makes a living off it. Yeah. And if you take the songs away from them that you wrote, he couldn't have any way of making a living.
Well, Bob, you know, right away, I was talking to him on the phone today, and he says, I love That's My Home. He thinks that's a great note. Oh, That's My Home, yeah. And, of course, Leeds He Down.

They keep putting that out. That's my home. But Louie made such a great record, haven't I? And that helps you. Yeah. With every issue of the records and everything. You're still getting the royalties as a whole. That's true, yeah. Yeah, that's true. And so, you know, we hardly scratch the surface on this thing. It's almost five o'clock. Anyway. Now I know when I got a big job.
